rows.selection_reason: With no prior experiments, the key uncertainty is whether the strongest multimodal combination (scgpt RNA encoder + ViT-L image encoder) with multiprofile aggregation yields a high-performing baseline. config_001 tests this 'strong multimodal' hypothesis using avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion—a simpler, more robust fusion strategy than transformer-based approaches. This is the best first experiment because: (1) it is likely to be near the top of the accuracy range, establishing a high reference point for the remaining 9 experiments; (2) if it performs well, subsequent experiments can efficiently explore variations (fusion type, aggregation, image encoder); if it underperforms, it signals that the architecture needs rethinking; (3) it avoids the extra cost of transformer aggregation while still testing the core multimodal hypothesis. Expected relative cost: high (ViT-L + scgpt + multiprofile processing), but moderate compared to transformer-aggregation configs like config_014 or config_032.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted → acc 0.542), the evidence is extremely sparse and the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal combination is actually contributing over a strong unimodal baseline. config_036 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, avgpool) is the cleanest ablation of config_001: it keeps the same RNA encoder (scgpt), same profile setting (multiprofile), and same aggregation (avgpool), removing only the image branch and fusion. If RNA-only achieves accuracy close to 0.542, the image modality is not adding value and I should pivot to cheaper RNA-focused or image-focused configs for the remaining 8 experiments. If it drops substantially, multimodal is confirmed as the right direction and I can then explore fusion/aggregation/encoder variants within the multimodal family. Expected cost: roughly 1.5–2.0 GPU hours (no ViT-L image forward/backward), making it cheaper than config_001 while answering the highest-leverage design question early in the budget.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, scgpt+imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.542 acc but only marginally beats RNA-only config_036 (0.530 acc, 0.515 F1), and actually loses on F1 (0.483 vs 0.515). This suggests the current weighted fusion strategy may not be effectively combining the two modalities. Question: config_006 isolates the fusion mechanism by switching from weighted to concat while keeping everything else identical (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, multiprofile). This is the cleanest single-variable ablation from our best result. Why this experiment: With 7 experiments remaining, I need to determine whether multimodal fusion can meaningfully outperform RNA-only before investing in more complex variants (transformer aggregation, different encoders). If concat fusion improves accuracy/F1, it validates the multimodal direction and guides subsequent experiments toward better fusion+aggregation combos. If it doesn't, the bottleneck is elsewhere (aggregation or image encoder), and I can pivot. Expected cost: similar to config_001 (~2.9 GPU hours), since the architecture is identical except for the fusion layer.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is the best at 0.542 acc, and weighted fusion clearly beats concat (0.542 vs 0.518). The only untested dimension on this top configuration is the aggregation method—avgpool has been used in all three completed experiments, so we have no evidence about whether transformer aggregation could better capture inter-profile relationships. Question: Does replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation (while keeping the proven scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion stack) improve validation accuracy? This is the highest-uncertainty, highest-potential-reward single-variable change from the current best. Rationale: With 6 experiments remaining, exploiting the strongest configuration while probing the one untested architectural axis (aggregation) is the most efficient use of the next slot. Expected relative cost: moderate-to-high (~4–5 GPU hrs), since transformer attention over multiple profiles adds compute over avgpool but is still lighter than the concat-fusion variant (7.18 hrs); this is justified because the expected accuracy gain from better profile interaction modeling is substantial.

Evidence: The best config so far (config_001: scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, multiprofile) achieves 0.542 accuracy, but the RNA-only baseline (config_036: scgpt + avgpool) reaches 0.530, meaning the image modality contributes only ~1.2%. All multimodal tests have used imagenet_vit_l, leaving the image encoder choice unexplored. Weighted fusion clearly outperforms concat (0.542 vs 0.518), and avgpool beats transformer aggregation (0.542 vs 0.520) with this RNA encoder. Question: Will switching the image encoder to ResNet50 (which captures different morphological/spatial features than a ViT) improve the multimodal contribution beyond the current 1.2% gain, while keeping all other settings at their best-performing values? Why this is the best next experiment: It is a clean single-variable change from the current best, directly testing whether the modest image benefit is encoder-specific. ResNet50 is substantially smaller than ViT-L (~23M vs ~300M params), so the expected training cost is lower—roughly 1.5–2.5 GPU hours vs. the 2.94 for config_001—making it a cost-efficient exploration. If it matches or beats 0.542, we gain a cheaper best config; if it underperforms, we confirm ViT-L is the right image encoder and can focus remaining budget on other dimensions (RNA encoder, profile setting).

Evidence: config_001 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, multiprofile) is the best at 0.5420 acc, and all completed experiments used scgpt as the RNA encoder. The only other RNA encoder tested (in rna_only config_036) was also scgpt, so we have zero evidence on whether scvi_n200 or pca_n2000 could match or exceed scgpt in the multimodal setting. Question: Does swapping scgpt for scvi_n200 in the best-performing multimodal configuration (imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) maintain or improve accuracy? This directly tests the RNA encoder axis, which is the most important unexplored dimension given that all top results used scgpt. If scvi_n200 performs comparably, it likely trains cheaper (VAE vs. transformer-based encoder), improving the accuracy-per-GPU-hour ratio. If it underperforms, we confirm scgpt is the right choice and can focus remaining budget on other axes (e.g., single profile, resnet50 variants). Expected cost: moderate, roughly 2.0–2.5 GPU hours (scvi_n200 is lighter than scgpt, but imagenet_vit_l and multiprofile aggregation keep it in the same ballpark as config_001's 2.94 hrs). This is the best use of experiment 6 because it exploits the strongest configuration while reducing uncertainty on a high-impact design choice, leaving 4 experiments to exploit whichever RNA encoder wins.

The dominant finding is that switching the RNA encoder from scgpt to scvi_n200 (config_026) produced a large jump to 0.706 accuracy, far exceeding all scgpt-based configs (~0.52–0.54). With only 3 experiments remaining after this one, the priority is to exploit the scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted-fusion + multiprofile combination and test whether the aggregation method can be improved. config_027 is a single-variable extension of the best config, replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation. While transformer was slightly worse than avgpool in the scgpt experiments (0.520 vs 0.542), scvi_n200's learned latent representation may interact differently with attention-based aggregation, potentially capturing richer inter-profile relationships. This is the highest-information next step: if it improves, we have a stronger champion; if it does not, we confirm avgpool is optimal and can focus remaining budget on other axes (e.g., image encoder or singleprofile). Expected cost is moderate, roughly 5–6 GPU hours (comparable to config_026's 4.82 h with a small overhead for the transformer aggregation layer), keeping total spend well within budget.

Evidence: The dominant finding is that scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile dramatically outperforms all scgpt-based configs (0.725 vs ~0.54). Within this family, transformer aggregation (config_027, 0.7250) beats avgpool (config_026, 0.7062) by ~2%, and weighted fusion has consistently outperformed concat in all prior comparisons (e.g., config_001 vs config_006). Question: config_048 tests the one remaining untested combination within our proven best architecture—scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat—directly probing whether concat fusion might complement transformer aggregation differently than it does with avgpool. Why this is the best use of experiment 8: It is the lowest-risk, highest-information exploitation of our strongest result, testing the last untested variable in the top-performing family. Expected cost is moderate (~3.5–4 GPU hrs), comparable to config_027 (3.60 hrs) since the architecture is identical except for the fusion operation. Even if it does not surpass config_027, it definitively closes the fusion question for this architecture, allowing the final experiment to be directed at a more exploratory direction (e.g., singleprofile or an alternative image encoder) with full confidence about the current best.

Evidence: config_027 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile) is the clear best at 0.725 accuracy, and the scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l encoder pair is strongly validated. The only major untested dimension with these top encoders is the profile setting (singleprofile vs multiprofile). Question: config_022 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted, singleprofile) tests whether removing the aggregation step and processing a single profile directly can match or exceed the multiprofile+transformer pipeline. This is valuable because singleprofile eliminates the aggregation bottleneck entirely, and with the strong scvi_n200 encoder the per-profile signal may already be sufficient. Why this is the best use: with only 1 experiment remaining after this one, I need to either find a configuration that beats 0.725 or confirm the ceiling. Singleprofile is the only structurally different unexplored axis with the proven best encoders. It is also expected to be cheaper (~2.5–3.0 GPU hours vs 3.60 for config_027) since it skips the transformer aggregation step, improving the cost-accuracy tradeoff if it performs comparably. If it underperforms, it confirms multiprofile+transformer is essential and locks in config_027 as the final answer.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer + weighted as the optimal architecture (config_027: 0.725 acc), with imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder. The only remaining untested variable within this top-performing family is the image encoder: config_033 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + multiprofile + transformer + weighted) tests whether the smaller resnet50 backbone can match or approach vit_l's performance when paired with the superior scvi_n200 RNA encoder. From the scgpt comparisons (config_001 vs config_009), vit_l outperformed resnet50 by ~1.7%, but scvi_n200's stronger representations may interact differently with the image modality. This is the best use of the final experiment because: (1) it tests the one remaining design choice in the proven-best architecture, (2) if resnet50 matches vit_l, it offers a cheaper alternative for deployment, and (3) if it underperforms, it definitively confirms config_027 as the optimal configuration. Expected cost is moderate (~2.5–3.5 GPU hours), slightly cheaper than config_027 since resnet50 has fewer parameters than ViT-L, keeping total budget reasonable.
